behaviour.summary: The showtimes model carries a single flag for whether seating is allocated, and the vendor documents the limitation candidly: the API does not indicate whether that allocation is automatic or manual. A caller learns that seats matter and not whether it must choose them.
behaviour.testable_as: The published Showtimes model exposes an allocated-seating boolean and no member distinguishing automatic from manual allocation.
behaviour.consequence_for_agents: The first branch in any seat-selection routine — do I pick, or am I given — cannot be taken from the data, so an agent must guess or ask a human, at the exact moment the point of an agent was not to. CHANGEOVER makes the manner of an Occasion part of the assertion set the etag is computed over, so a change in it is a change the consumer can detect.

half_life_basis: A documented limitation is the kind of claim a vendor closes deliberately and then announces; the page carries its own Updated about 1 year ago stamp, so it is neither fresh nor abandoned. Half a year.

citation.quote: The MX Showtimes API currently only indicates whether a showtime's seating is allocated or not—not whether allocation is automatic or manual.

notes: movieXchange Limited publicly describes itself as a company of Vista Group International Ltd. Recorded because the aggregation seat between exhibitor and ticketer is commercially occupied, which is a constraint on this project's positioning, not a relationship: see corpus/README.md.
